questions.question: Which stakeholder group listed on page 3 is most directly responsible for translating client requirements into a technical design for the system?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The figure shows System architects positioned between requirements and software developers, indicating they translate requirements into technical design. [Page 3]

questions.question: According to the description on page 30, what is the primary purpose of developing a prototype in a client‑server project?

options.A: To finalize the user interface before coding begins
options.B: To obtain performance metrics for the final system
options.C: To allow stakeholders to experiment with the system and provide requirement feedback
options.D: To replace the need for a formal feasibility study

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Prototyping involves creating an executable model for stakeholders to experiment with and feed back requirement changes. [Page 30]

---

questions.question: In the feasibility‑study guidance referenced on page 4, which of the following indicates that a project should likely be abandoned?

options.A: All stakeholder questions receive a “yes” answer
options.B: The cost‑benefit analysis shows a positive return
options.C: Any of the listed feasibility questions is answered “no”
options.D: The prototype meets all user expectations

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The text states that if the answer to any feasibility question is “no,” the project should probably not go ahead. [Page 4]

questions.question: The excerpt on page 28 mentions “architectural components that are reused.” Which architectural concept does this statement best illustrate?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Reusing architectural components reflects the modular design principle that promotes component reuse across system modules. [Page 28]

questions.question: Based on the stakeholder diagram on page 3, which two groups are most likely to have overlapping interests in the functional requirements of the system?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Both software developers and system architects work closely on how functional requirements are implemented, indicating overlapping interests. [Page 3]

questions.question: Dijkstra’s 1972 article “The Humble Programmer” (referenced on page 36) is cited in the context of client‑server architecture primarily to emphasize which principle?

options.A: The need for rigorous testing before deployment
options.B: The importance of modest, maintainable code in system development
options.C: The advantage of high‑performance hardware in server design
options.D: The role of formal specifications in requirements gathering

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Dijkstra’s “Humble Programmer” stresses modest, maintainable code, a principle relevant to building reliable client‑server systems. [Page 36]

questions.question: When evaluating the high‑level system architecture described on page 28, which aspect would most directly affect the distribution of functions across modules?

options.A: The programming language chosen for implementation
options.B: The identification of reusable architectural components
options.C: The number of end‑users expected to access the system
options.D: The budget allocated for hardware procurement

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Recognizing reusable components influences how functions are allocated among system modules. [Page 28]

questions.question: According to the prototyping process on page 30, which statement best captures the role of end‑users during prototype evaluation?

options.A: They write the final code for the system.
options.B: They verify that the prototype meets performance benchmarks.
options.C: They experiment with the prototype and suggest requirement changes.
options.D: They approve the final system architecture.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] End‑users interact with the prototype to test its suitability and provide feedback on requirements. [Page 30]

questions.question: Referring to the stakeholder diagram on page 3, which pair of roles is most likely to be involved in defining the system’s non‑functional requirements such as reliability and security?

options.D: System client engineers and Client engineers

questions.explanation: [Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] System architects design overall system qualities, while software developers implement them, making them central to non‑functional requirements. [Page 3]
